steps.answer: The catalog has no records on how honeybees choose a nest site, and the public-domain passages I read don't answer the question. The 1852 guide (A complete guide to the mystery and management of bees, p. 25) describes gathering a swarm's queens onto a cloth, and p. 9 advises on hive sizes for swarms. Neither says where bees settle. From general knowledge, not from these sources, scout bees search for cavities of roughly a few liters with small entrances, and the swarm decides collectively through waggle-dance advocacy. Modern books such as The honey bee: understanding the ultimate engineer (2020) and The wisdom of the hive (1995) probably cover this, but I haven't read them.
